explanations: There is no defect. Both account locks are taken before the balances are read, and the read, the funds check and applyTransfer all happen while both locks are held, so no other transfer touching either account can interleave between check and write. Locks are always acquired in sorted id order, so two opposite transfers (A->B and B->A) cannot deadlock. KeyedMutex chains each waiter on the previous tail, so waiters run in FIFO order, and the map entry is removed only if no later waiter has replaced the tail. Both releases sit in finally blocks, so validation errors still free the locks. This assumes a single process owns these accounts; that is a deployment constraint, not a bug in the code shown.

transfer() sorts the ids into firstId/secondId before locking, so both requests lock A first. Whichever gets A first also takes B, finishes, and releases; the other then proceeds. Deadlock needs opposite acquisition order, which the sort prevents. Locks cover both accounts, not just the source, and KeyedMutex waits rather than failing.

Each acquire() awaits the previous tail and installs a new tail that resolves only after its own release is called. T2 waits on T1's tail, T3 waits on T2's, giving FIFO order. Nothing lets T3 skip ahead, and T2 and T3 cannot overlap because T3's previous is T2's tail.

releaseSecond() runs in the inner finally and releaseFirst() in the outer finally, so both run regardless of the error. Neither try block has a catch, so the error is rethrown to the caller rather than swallowed.
